reasoning: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a well-known, thoroughly debunked myth. Modern neuroimaging technologies, such as functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) and Positron Emission Tomography (PET) scans, clearly show that virtually all parts of the brain have a determined function and are active throughout the day, even during sleep. From an evolutionary perspective, the brain represents a massive energy drain; if 90% of it were dormant and unused, natural selection would have eliminated this highly inefficient design. Additionally, any areas of the brain that genuinely go unused due to damage or lack of activity undergo rapid degeneration (atrophy).
